questions.question: A technician is diagnosing a 5-volt reference circuit that reads 0 volts at multiple sensors. What is the best first step?
options: Replace all sensors on the circuit
Check for a shorted sensor or wire pulling the reference voltage down
questions.explanation: A shared 5-volt reference can be pulled low by one shorted sensor or wire. Disconnecting sensors one at a time may help isolate the fault. Replacing all sensors without testing is not proper diagnosis. ---

questions.category: E2: Gasoline Fuel Delivery and Injection Systems
questions.question: A gasoline direct injection engine has a long crank and low high-pressure fuel rail reading. What should be checked?
options: Low-pressure supply and high-pressure pump operation
questions.explanation: Direct injection systems use low- and high-pressure fuel sides. A fault in either can reduce rail pressure. Diagnosis should follow pressure and command data. ---

questions.question: A coil-on-plug engine has a misfire on cylinder 4. The coil is swapped to cylinder 2 and the misfire moves. What is the likely fault?
questions.explanation: If the misfire follows the coil, the coil is suspect. Swapping components is a useful confirmation test. The spark plug and circuit should still be inspected. ---

questions.question: A vehicle has a stored P0171 lean code. Which data is most useful to review first?
options: Fuel trims and oxygen sensor data
questions.explanation: Fuel trims show how the PCM is correcting mixture. Oxygen sensor data helps confirm lean or rich feedback. Diagnosis should use live data before replacing parts. ---

questions.category: E5: Gasoline Intake and Exhaust Systems
questions.question: A restricted catalytic converter may cause:
options: Loss of power at higher RPM
questions.explanation: Exhaust restriction limits engine breathing. The symptom often worsens under load or high RPM. Backpressure testing can confirm the restriction. ---
